[Math, Lesson #/Title] Lesson 14: Divide Three-Digit Numbers
[Math, Standard] 4.NR.2.4 – Solve real-life division problems (up to 4-digit dividends, 1-digit divisors with remainders). I can divide up to three-digit dividends by one-digit divisors.
[Math, Success Criteria] I can set up and find the quotient of the division problem using an efficient strategy (area model or partial quotients). I can double-check my work using multiplication and addition
[Math, Retrieval Activator, Day 1] "Which Remainder Rule?" (Card Sort / Corner Kick)
[Math, Retrieval Activator, Day 1] Ask students to quickly signal or write on a whiteboard whether they should Drop It, Add 1 (Round Up), or Use the Remainder.
[Math, Retrieval Activator, Day 2] "Spot the Error & Fix the Check"
[Math, Retrieval Activator, Day 3] The remainder can be larger than the divisor. (Lie — remainder must always be smaller!)
[Math, Vocabulary & Strategy] NEW dividend, divisor
[Math, Vocabulary & Strategy] REVIEW divide, division, estimate (noun), estimate (verb), multiple, quotient, remainder
[Math, Daily Instructional Plan] Monday: Session 1
[Science, Lesson #/Title] Unit 3: Forecasting the Weather Properties of Water
[Science, Standard] S4E3. I can use investigations and models to explain how water changes form.
[Science, Success Criteria] Identify the three states of water (solid ice, liquid water, and gas water vapor).
[Science, Success Criteria] Explain how adding heat causes ice to melt into water and water to evaporate into water vapor.
[Science, Success Criteria] Explain how cooling/removing heat causes water vapor to condense into liquid water and water to freeze into ice.
[Science, Vocabulary & Strategy] Condensation Evaporation Gas Liquid Matter Solid Temperature Water Vapor
[Science, Questions] The addition of heat energy causes matter to melt.
[Science, Questions] The removal of heat energy causes matter to freeze.
